group.name: Hudson Valley Mutual Aid
group.purpose: Neighbors across the mid-Hudson Valley meeting each other's needs: sharing what we have, asking for what we need, and getting ready together for storms, floods, smoke and outages.
group.description: We're a network of neighbors, not a charity. Post a request when you need something, an offer when you have something to share, and map the apple trees, fridges and free pantries around you. Gifts, loans and trades only, never sales.

menu.page:
A note from the Weavers. This is a network of neighbors. Post a request when you need something, an offer when you have something to share, and put apple trees, fridges, and pantries on the map.

Una nota de las tejedoras. Somos una red de vecinas y vecinos. Pide lo que necesitas, ofrece lo que puedes compartir, y marca en el mapa los árboles frutales, el refrigerador comunitario y las despensas.

How to use this network. Ask. Offer. Map a resource. Join your local town space.

Newburgh · Kingston & Rondout · Saugerties & Esopus Creek · Poughkeepsie & Arlington

views.page:
Ten trusted neighbors each have 100 tokens. Each token is $5 of the $5,000 pool. Spread them across the proposals. You can see the totals move while voting is open.

Diez vecinas y vecinos tienen 100 fichas cada quien. Cada ficha vale $5 de un fondo de $5,000. Se ven los totales mientras la votación está abierta.

views.page: Five steps. When you finish, you're ready to join in.

agreements.title: Solidarity, not charity.
agreements.description: Everyone has needs and everyone has something to give.

agreements.title: Protect each other's privacy.
agreements.description: Share exact addresses in DMs, not in posts. Ask before posting photos of people or homes.

agreements.title: Close the loop.
agreements.description: Mark your post fulfilled and thank who helped, so the network can see what's working.

posts.title: Convertible car seat for my 2-year-old
posts.details: Daycare will not take him in the old one. If you have a convertible seat your kid outgrew, we can pick it up.

comments.text: I have a Graco Extend2Fit, outgrown, never in a crash. Messaging you.
Nia brought it over this afternoon. He is in it tomorrow. Thank you.

posts.title: Beds for 3 kids (ages 6, 9, 12)
posts.details: We got here in August and the kids are still on the floor. Twin or bunk is fine. I can help carry.

comments.text: A Kingston family has bunks. I can haul them Saturday.

posts.title: Kitchen table that seats 5
posts.details: We are eating on the floor too. Nothing fancy. A table and a few chairs would change the evenings.

comments.text: I can build one from shop scraps this week. What height works for the kids?

posts.title: Winter coats, kids sizes 6, 9, 12
posts.details: Coats are the piece we still do not have. Sizes 6, 9, and 12. Used is perfect. The first hard frost is close.

comments.text: I have a size 9 puffer and a size 6 raincoat. They are clean. I can leave them with Rosa.
Drop them at the fridge porch. I will text Farid.

posts.title: Dari speaker for a school meeting Thursday
posts.details: The school meeting is Thursday and I do not want to miss what they are asking of us. If you speak Dari, I can meet you there.

comments.text: I can come Thursday. Send me the time and the school name.

posts.title: Ride to a job interview in Fishkill
posts.details: Interview is Thursday morning in Fishkill. I do not have a car and the bus gets me there late. I can chip in gas.

comments.text: My car is in the shop or I would take you.
I can do it. I will be at Broadway and Henry at 8.
Got the job!

posts.title: Borrow a drill to hang shelves
posts.details: Need a drill and a few bits for shelves tonight or tomorrow. I will bring it back to the shed.

comments.text: Grab mine from the shed. It is the blue case on the left. No need to ask Jorge, I already told him.
Blue case is still there. Put it back on the left when you are done.

posts.title: Grab bars installed in my bathroom
posts.details: The tub is getting harder. If someone can put up two grab bars, the hardware can be mine or yours.

comments.text: I can do it Thursday. I will bring the bars so you do not have to shop.

posts.title: 2 more drivers for elder check-ins during storms
posts.details: When the next nor'easter hits I still need two more drivers to call and visit elders in Saugerties, especially along the creek. An hour, a phone, and a car.

posts.title: Generator to borrow for the warming hub
posts.details: The church hall on Church Street will be the warming hub if the power goes. A quiet generator for two nights would cover the cots and the radio.

comments.text: The farm has a small one. It is loud. Yours if nobody has a quieter one.

posts.title: Working rototiller to borrow for a weekend
posts.details: I want to open two more beds before the garlic workday. A working tiller for a weekend, I will return it full of gas.

comments.text: The library does not have one yet. If the fundraiser proposal passes we could buy one and keep it at the shed.

posts.title: Help carrying a couch to a 3rd-floor walkup, Saturday
posts.details: A neighbor on Crown Street is giving a couch to someone on the third floor. We need two more people Saturday morning. No truck, just stairs.

posts.title: Box fans for elders without AC (heat wave)
posts.details: Checking on elders in the last heat wave. Several apartments have no AC. Box fans, working, any color.

comments.text: I have six box fans in the garage from the old shop.
I can bring two more and help Walt drop them off.

posts.title: Crib or pack-n-play for a client due next week
posts.details: A client is due next week and does not have a safe place for the baby to sleep. Crib or pack-n-play, I can pick up.

comments.text: I think there is a pack-n-play in the shed. Checking tonight.

posts.title: Rides to dialysis, Tue/Thu mornings, for my neighbor
posts.details: My neighbor on Broadway has dialysis Tuesday and Thursday mornings. One ride a week from anyone with a car would cover the gap the medical van misses.

comments.text: I can take Tuesdays. I am already headed that direction for work.
Thursdays work for me through the end of the month.

posts.title: Kitchen faucet leaking, anyone handy?
posts.details: The kitchen faucet started dripping hard this morning. I cannot get the water to stop all the way. If you are handy and free today, I can make tea.

posts.title: Help moving boxes off the garage floor before Friday's rain
posts.details: The last storm pushed the creek over the curb on Partition Street and into the garage. I cannot lift the heavy boxes. If two people can move them onto shelves, I will have coffee on.

comments.text: Tomas is running a truck Saturday, but I can come by Thursday evening to lift the heavy ones.

posts.title: Sump pump or wet vac, the basement took water again
posts.details: Four inches in the basement after the last storm, right under the water heater. I need a pump or a wet vac for a day so it does not sit there. I can pick it up in Saugerties.

comments.text: The shed has a wet vac. Yellow shop vac, bottom shelf. Bring it back emptied.

posts.title: 24 ft ladder + pole fruit picker, borrow anytime
posts.details: Both live in my garage in Kingston. Borrow them whenever, including for gleaning. Bring the ladder back with all the parts.

comments.text: Ladder is back on your porch. Thank you, the high pears would still be in the tree.

posts.title: Day-old bread every Friday, 2–4pm
posts.details: The bakery lets me take what is left. Fridays 2 to 4 on Abeel Street in Rondout. Farid, there is a loaf with your name on it every week now.

posts.title: Free garlic to plant + kale and chard starts, 200+
posts.details: Forty heads of seed garlic and two hundred kale and chard starts on the farm table. Come take a flat or a head and get it in before the ground freezes. They were gone by the middle of the month.

posts.title: Apple butter, 24 jars
posts.details: Twenty-four jars from the Saugerties windfalls and the canning class. First come, bring a story if you want a second jar.

posts.title: Free bike tune-ups Sundays
posts.details: Sundays at Broadway and Union, bring the bike. Flats, brakes, and gears. Parts at cost if I have them, otherwise we make a list.

posts.title: Free algebra and calculus tutoring, Tuesdays
posts.details: Tuesdays after 4 at the library or a cafe. Algebra through calc. Parents, your kid can come. I got help when I needed it.

posts.title: Brakes and oil changes, free, bring parts
posts.details: I was a mechanic before we moved. Brakes and oil changes, free, you bring the parts. It feels good to be useful here.

posts.title: Truck + muscle for moves, most Saturdays
posts.details: Truck is free most Saturdays. Moves inside the valley, no dump runs. Message me the night before.

posts.title: Help with rental assistance applications
posts.details: I know the rental assistance forms and which office actually answers. Bring your lease and a recent bill. English or Spanish.

posts.title: Meal train for new parents
posts.details: If you just had a baby, or your neighbor did, I will set up a meal train. Newburgh and nearby. Tell me dietary needs.

posts.title: 6 box fans
posts.details: Six working box fans from the old shop. They all went to Lin's elder list during the heat wave.

posts.title: Canning class, bring 6 jars
posts.details: Next session uses the apples if you still have them. Bring 6 jars. The water-bath kit is in the tool shed.

posts.title: Ham radio license study group
posts.details: Technician license study group, a few evenings. Useful when the cell network is down in a storm. No equipment required to start.

posts.title: Box of 40 N95 masks for smoke days
posts.details: Forty N95s from a clinic surplus. Take a few for your household before the next smoke day. I am keeping ten for the elder visits.

posts.title: Saturday truck for moving furniture off the floor
posts.details: Before the creek comes up I can haul a load or move a couch and a mattress upstairs. Poughkeepsie and Saugerties. Message me Friday night with the address.

comments.text: Our block off Main Street floods at the corner. Can you take two mattresses up Saturday?

posts.title: Apple + Bartlett pear trees, glean anytime
posts.details: Two trees in the yard near Partition and Main. I cannot climb anymore. Take what you need, just leave me a dozen.

comments.text: I cannot climb anymore. Take what you need, just leave me a dozen.
Bea, these are gorgeous. Can the crew come through one morning? I will message you.

posts.title: Pawpaw patch on the public strip
posts.details: Pawpaws on the strip by Block Park in Rondout. Public side of the fence, ripe now, bring a bag and a soft touch.

posts.title: Two quince trees along the alley
posts.details: Two quince trees on the alley side of Carson and Lander. The owner said the crew is welcome. They ripen in a wave.

posts.title: Concord grape arbor, ask the owner first
posts.details: A long arbor of Concord grapes at Smith and Parker. The fruit hangs over the sidewalk. Knock and ask, they have said yes before.

posts.title: Cortland and Northern Spy apple trees, ripe Sept–Nov
posts.details: Old apple trees in the front yard, ripe September through November. Take a bag. Please do not climb the fence.

posts.title: Newburgh community fridge, open 24/7
posts.details: The fridge on the Liberty Street porch is open all night. Take what you need, leave what you can. It is full of Hannah's apples this week.

posts.title: Little Free Pantry
posts.details: Dry goods cupboard next to the canning porch. Pasta, rice, and jars when we have them.

posts.title: Poughkeepsie urban farm, free produce Saturdays
posts.details: The half acre is open Saturdays for anyone to take produce. Bring a bag.

posts.title: Newburgh tool shed (hours, how to borrow)
posts.details: Garage shed on South William Street. Borrowing works like a library: write your name, the tool, and when it comes back. Open most evenings.

posts.title: Pressure washer
posts.details: Pressure washer lives at the Newburgh shed. Good for sidewalks and not for paint. Back in two days.

posts.title: Wet tile saw
posts.details: Wet tile saw at the shed. Messy, so use it in the driveway. Ask Jorge before you take it off the stand.

posts.title: Post-hole digger + 2 shovels
posts.details: Post-hole digger and two shovels. The digger is heavier than it looks. Bring it back cleaned.

posts.title: Water-bath canning kit
posts.details: Big pot, rack, and jar lifter. Used for the apple butter class. It lives at the shed between classes.

posts.title: Saugerties Gleaning Day
posts.details: Meet at Bea's apple and pear trees. Bring bags, gloves, and a ladder if you have one. Half the fruit goes to the Newburgh fridge.

posts.title: Fix-it Clinic: bikes and small appliances
posts.details: Bikes and small appliances at the Newburgh shed. Jorge is on appliances, Dev is on bikes. Bring the thing and the story of what it used to do.

posts.title: Sandbag Day at the Poughkeepsie farm
posts.details: Fill bags for households that flood first. 9 to noon at the urban farm. Shovels on site, gloves if you have them.

comments.text: Sandbag Day is coming up. Tibet, you still in for the morning shift?

posts.title: Newburgh Potluck & Skill Swap
posts.details: Sunday evening at the waterfront picnic tables. Bring a dish if you can and one thing you know how to do. Folding tables are spoken for.

posts.title: Wildfire smoke & first aid class
posts.details: How to seal a room, when to leave, and the first aid that shows up on smoke days. Saugerties library meeting room.

posts.title: Garlic Planting Workday
posts.details: Beds, starts, and garlic at the Poughkeepsie farm. Beginners welcome. We stop at noon and eat whatever is ready.

posts.title: Welcome! Introduce yourself here
posts.details: Say where you live and one thing you could share. This thread stays at the top so new people can find us.

comments.text: Hannah, Kingston and Rondout. I glean fruit that would otherwise hit the sidewalk.
Marcus, Poughkeepsie. Seedlings if you have a pot.

posts.title: Should we start a tool library?
posts.details: My garage is already half a library. If we name it and write things down, more people can borrow without asking me first. What would you want on the shelf?

posts.title: Gleaning Day recap: 140 lbs!
posts.details: 140 pounds of apples and pears off Bea's trees. Half went to the Newburgh fridge, 30 pounds to Ellie's canning class. Thanks Tibet for the ladder.

comments.text: The fridge was full by evening. People kept coming back with bags.
You left me my dozen, and the trees look relieved. Come back for the last pears.

posts.title: What's in your outage kit?
posts.details: Radio, water, meds, a way to charge a phone. What do you actually have, and what do you wish a neighbor had?

posts.title: Rent hikes on Crown Street, tenants meeting?
posts.details: Several buildings on Crown got notices the same week. If you rent nearby and want a meeting, say so here and I will find a room.

posts.title: What's in season right now?
posts.details: Pawpaws are ready. Quince need another week in the shade. What are you seeing in your alley?

comments.text: Bartletts on my tree are still hard. Give them a week.
Las manzanas de Mill Street ya están buenas. Pueden pasar.
The pawpaws by Block Park dropped fruit on the path this morning. It is time.
I will take a bag of pawpaws if someone is already going.

posts.title: How should we spend the $2,400 from the fall fundraiser?
posts.details: The block party raised $2,400. One choice. Voting closes in a few days. We need 20% of the network for quorum.

posts.title: Move the Newburgh potluck to Sundays?
posts.details: Weeknights were leaving out the night-shift folks. Sundays 5 to 8?

posts.title: Welcome Home kit for Farid's family
posts.details: A few of us are pulling together beds, a table, coats, and a Dari speaker for Farid, his wife, and their three kids. Add yourself if you can carry something.

posts.title: Busco cuna para mi bebé, nace en diciembre
posts.details: Mi bebé nace en diciembre y no tenemos cuna. Si alguien tiene una, o un corralito, la paso a buscar. Gracias.

comments.text: Creo que hay un corralito en el cobertizo. Lo reviso y te escribo.

posts.title: Clases de inglés gratis los sábados / Free English classes Saturdays
posts.details: Sábados por la mañana en Newburgh, inglés práctico: escuela, clínica, trabajo. English for school, clinic, and work. Free.

posts.title: Taller: cómo prepararse para las tormentas (en español)
posts.details: Una hora en español: agua, documentos, a quién llamar, cómo llenar sacos. Traigan a quien necesite oírlo.

posts.title: ¿Alguien sabe de ayuda para pagar la renta?
posts.details: Nos subieron la renta y no sé por dónde empezar. ¿Alguien ha pedido ayuda y le contestaron?

comments.text: Sí. Trae el contrato y un recibo. Te ayudo con la solicitud en español o en inglés, the county rental assistance office on Market Street is the one that actually answers. Puedo verte esta semana.

posts.title: Árbol de manzanas, pueden tomar lo que necesiten
posts.details: Manzanas en Mill y Cannon. Están buenas. Toquen la puerta, o pasen si la reja está abierta. Dejen unas cuantas.

posts.title: Cucumbers and green beans from my garden
posts.details: More cucumbers and green beans than we can eat. A box on the steps Saturday morning.

posts.title: Ride to Stewart airport Friday at 5am
posts.details: Flight Friday, need to be at Stewart by 5am. I can give gas money and I am a quiet passenger.

comments.text: I am up anyway. I will take you if you are at Broadway and Henry at 3:50.

posts.title: New compressor + shade cover for the Newburgh fridge
posts.details: The compressor is loud and tired, and the porch bakes in the afternoon. A new compressor and a shade cover keep food safe in September.

posts.title: Cots and blankets for the winter warming hub
posts.details: Twelve cots and blankets for the hall we open when the power fails. They stay in the Ready Hudson closet the rest of the year.

posts.title: Bilingual storm-prep flyers + door-knocking
posts.details: Flyers in Spanish and English, and a Saturday of door-knocking in Newburgh and Poughkeepsie before the first big nor'easter.

posts.title: Interpreter stipends (Dari, Spanish, Haitian Creole) for school and clinic visits
posts.details: Small stipends so neighbors who interpret at schools and clinics are not doing it unpaid every week.

posts.title: Poughkeepsie seed library
posts.details: Jars, labels, and a shelf at the farm for seeds people already save. Anyone can take a packet and bring some back.

posts.title: Bike trailer for hauling gleaned fruit
posts.details: A trailer behind a bike moves apples without waiting on a truck. It would live with the gleaning crew.

posts.title: Kids' bike repair camp
posts.details: Two Saturdays where kids learn to fix a flat and leave with a working bike. Parts are the budget.

messages.text: This is the town thread. Say hello when you arrive.
Gleaning crew is meeting at Bea's next week. Details are in events.
Farm stand Saturday. Kale starts are free until they are gone.
Nor'easter is on the weekend maps. Check the Ready Hudson space.
If your rent notice came this month, look at the Crown Street thread.
Who has a truck Saturday besides me? Couch on Crown, third floor.
I can drive elders that morning if the couch is covered.
Friday bread is two loaves heavier than usual. Come by Abeel Street.
N95s are in a box at my porch. Take a few before the next smoke day.
Join requests: if you asked to join and have not heard, we are reading them today.
Canning class still has four open seats.
Pawpaws by Block Park are dropping. Bags in the gleaning thread.
Fridge was empty at dawn and full by noon. That is a good day.
¿Alguien tiene una cuna pequeña? Publiqué un pedido.
Tool shed is open tonight until 8. Drill bits are restocked.
Meal train for a family on Johnston Street starts Thursday. Soup is covered, we need two dinners.
Apple butter is gone. Thank you for taking it to people who will actually eat it.
Clase de inglés este sábado, misma esquina de siempre.
I can do Tuesday dialysis rides. I put it on Rosa's request.
Does anyone have a folding table that is not already promised to the potluck?
Fridge is FULL of Hannah's apples, come grab some 🍎
Taking 2 bags for canning class, thank you!
Anyone have a pack-n-play? Posted a request, client is due next week.
I think there is one in the shed, checking tonight.
can you bring the folding tables to the potluck Sunday?
Found it. Nia I will drop it by tomorrow 👍
Bread Friday is on. Two to four, Abeel Street side.
Fix-it clinic needs one more person who is not afraid of toasters.
If anyone is already going toward Fishkill Thursday morning, I posted a ride request.
Crown Street notices went up. Thread is in discussions if you want the meeting.
I can help carry the couch if it is after 10.
Early Stewart airport ride Friday if anyone is a morning person.
Ladder is back in the garage. Fruit picker too. Borrow either.
Loaf set aside for Farid's family. Tomás, it can ride with you.
Starts are on the table. Take a flat, leave the tray.
The bunks are in the kids' room. They made their beds before I finished tightening the frame.
Easiest haul of the month. Happy to do the table next if Jorge needs a truck.
¿Alguien ha pedido ayuda para la renta? Dejé una pregunta en discusiones.
Cucumbers on the steps until noon.
Las manzanas de Mill están listas. Pasen.
Sandbag Day is Saturday at the farm. Bring a shovel.
Faucet request is up. If you are nearby today I am home after 2.
Bea said yes to a morning. We need a tall ladder.
Ladder and the fruit picker are yours. I will drop them the night before.
I will take the bruised ones for apple butter. Leave the pretty ones for the fridge.
You all left the yard cleaner than you found it. That is new.
Quince in the Newburgh alley are close. Another week.
Concords are dropping. Ask at the house, then pick the sidewalk side.
I can take a crate to the fridge Friday on my way back from the bakery.
Quince need another week. Pawpaws do not.
Forecast is getting serious. Check the Sandbag Day event before the weekend.
Still short two drivers for elder checks. The request is up.
Smoke class is on the calendar. Tell elders who will not come to a website.
Fundraiser vote is open. Read the three options before you pick.
Farm generator is the backup. It is loud and it works.
Radio net check-in tonight at 7. If you have a handheld, say your call sign or just hello.
Submissions are in. Read the budgets before you move tokens.
Farid's interpreter proposal is the one I keep coming back to.
The cots and the purifiers are both winter. Hard to split them in my head.
Voting is open. You can see the totals move, so do not all wait until the last hour.
I did not put tokens on the fridge. Someone else should decide that one.
Tibet, your hundred are still sitting there when you want them.
Just joined. I am in Kingston and I love the pawpaw patches nobody admits to owning.
Acabo de entrar. Vivo en Poughkeepsie y puedo cuidar niños entre semana.
Beacon here. I have a truck on Sundays.
Joined from Hyde Park. I can help with clinic paperwork.
Just joined. I can translate Haitian Creole if you tell me the day.
Can I borrow the 24 ft ladder and the fruit picker for Bea's trees? Thursday morning.
Yes. I will leave both on the porch Wednesday night.
Got them. I will bring a friend to carry the ladder, it is a long one.
The picker is in the blue bag. Do not stand on the top rung, Bea will tell you the same thing.
140 pounds. Your ladder did the high pears.
Good. Leave it whenever.
Ladder back on your porch, thank you!
I posted the $2,400 question. Three options. Tell me if I missed one before votes pile up.
The radios are Walt's, the purifiers are what the elders actually ask me for.
The tool library option is Jorge's tiller and a few things we keep borrowing from his garage.
I am leaving it at three. More options and nobody finishes.
Can we add warming-hub supplies if the cots do not win the flow fund?
If I add it now I have to reset votes. I do not want to do that to people.
Agree. Mention it in the thread so people know the cots exist as the other pot of money.
I will. And I want the purifiers. I am not pretending otherwise.
Tibet, you still have not voted. People at the table will watch the bar move if you do it live.
Dev said his drill is at the shed. Is the shed open Saturday?
Jorge usually opens it by 10. I can meet you there if the door is locked.
Is the tool shed open Saturday?
Lin needs fans. I have six. Can you bring two more and help deliver?
Yes. I will be at your garage at 4.
Loaded. Saugerties first, then the apartments off Ulster Avenue.
All eight are in windows. Lin has the list of who still needs one.
The Graco is in my closet. It expires next year, never in a crash. Want it?
Yes. I am off at 1. I can come to you or you can come here, whichever is easier.
I will come to you. Send the address here, not on the post.
Apartment 2, the building with the blue door just off Main Street. I will meet you in the lot so you do not have to find the stairs.
In the lot. I see you.
He sat in it in the driveway and did not complain. That is a review. Thank you.
Bea, your apple post is the best thing on the map. Can we bring a small crew one morning?
Mornings, not afternoons. I nap. And leave me a dozen apples and a few pears.
Thursday morning, 9 to 11. We will stay in the yard, not the house.
The side gate sticks. Lift it. And do not let anyone stand on the top of that ladder.
Dozen apples and a bowl of pears are on your kitchen chair. The rest is already at the fridge.
I wrote a project so people can see the whole list, not five separate surprises. Want to read it before it goes up?
Yes. Please say we can help too. I do not want it to sound like we only receive.
Beds, a table, coats, and a Dari speaker for Thursday. I will add that you fix cars.
The lease says we cannot paint. Is that a problem for the table? It is only furniture.
Furniture is fine. Do not drill into the walls for the beds if the lease says so. Jorge will know.
The bunks are up. The kids are arguing about the top bed, which means it worked.
Jorge is bringing the table tomorrow. I will be there to carry.
I posted that I can do brakes. It felt right after the table arrived.
I can take you. Broadway and Henry at 8. Interview clothes are fine in the truck.
I will be on the corner. Thank you. I have been rehearsing answers out loud.
Outside. Take your time, we are early.
Good luck was the right thing to say. I got it.
